CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hypertension and palpitations.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
49-year-old male with longstanding hypertension since young age presents with ongoing management of blood pressure. Patient had an emergency room visit in March with high blood pressure and palpitations, which he attributes to consuming several cups of coffee without breakfast and believes was a panic attack. He has not experienced palpitations since that visit. Recently started on new medication Benicar HCT (40-25, containing hydrochlorothiazide) by new primary care doctor approximately one month ago. Patient checks blood pressure at home every morning, with readings ranging from 146-155 mmHg, not yet at goal. Patient reports attempting to reduce salt intake and tries to walk on treadmill when able. Currently on three antihypertensive medications at maximum doses with suboptimal blood pressure control. Potassium level one week ago was 4.0. No recent repeat labs obtained.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension since young age. Emergency room visit in March for elevated blood pressure and palpitations.

MEDICATIONS
Amlodipine 10 mg daily. Benicar HCT (hydrochlorothiazide). Spironolactone (newly initiated).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Positive family history of hypertension.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient attempts to reduce salt intake. Exercises by walking on treadmill when able.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart and lungs: clear to auscultation. Abdomen: soft, no tenderness to palpation. Extremities: no swelling in ankles or feet.

RESULTS
Potassium level from one week ago: 4.0.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Resistant hypertension on three maximum-dose medications with inadequate control. Spironolactone added to current regimen. Counseled on potential side effects including dizziness, possible gynecomastia (rare, 1 in 100), and electrolyte disturbances. Instructed on importance of hydration to prevent dehydration. Metabolic panel and blood pressure check needed in two weeks to monitor potassium and sodium levels. Counseled on lifestyle modifications including salt restriction (goal under 2000 mg/day, ideally 1500 mg/day), regular aerobic exercise (30 minutes most days), and increased potassium intake. Provided information on DASH diet and heart.org website. Follow-up appointment in two weeks. If inadequate response to spironolactone, will refer to resistant hypertension clinic for evaluation of secondary causes and consideration of procedure-based interventions such as renal denervation.
